subject: surgery
title: Mucocele, Pseudomyxoma Peritonei, and Appendicitis in Pregnancy

steps.tx: Progressive cystic dilatation of the vermiform appendix caused by chronic intraluminal accumulation of gelatinous, mucus-rich secretions is termed a **mucocele of appendix**. Mucoceles are categorized pathologically into four distinct entities: non-neoplastic retention cysts, mucosal hyperplasia, low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasms, and invasive mucinous adenocarcinomas. While simple retention cysts stem from faecolith obstruction, true mucinous neoplasms demonstrate autonomous neoplastic mucin production.
steps.say: A mucocele of the appendix is cystic dilatation from mucus accumulation, ranging from benign retention cysts to mucinous neoplasms.

vis.alt: Gross surgical specimen of a massively distended, glassy translucent mucocele of the appendix.
vis.caption: Mucocele of the appendix: marked cystic distension of the appendiceal lumen filled with thick mucin. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: On cross-sectional computed tomography, an appendiceal mucocele appears as a well-circumscribed, round or tubular, low-attenuation cystic mass in the right lower quadrant, characteristically exhibiting curved mural calcification known as the porcelain appendix. Extreme care must be exercised during surgical manipulation to completely prevent iatrogenic capsular rupture. Unintentional spillage of neoplastic mucin into the peritoneal cavity seeds epithelial cells that produce catastrophic **pseudomyxoma peritonei**.
steps.say: CT demonstrates a tubular cystic mass with mural calcification, which must be handled delicately to prevent peritoneal mucin spillage.

vis.alt: Pathological diagram showing appendiceal mucinous neoplasm with abundant gelatinous mucin pools and peritoneal implants.
vis.caption: Appendiceal mucinous neoplasm: epithelial mucin secretion with potential for extensive transcoelomic dissemination. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: The devastating peritoneal syndrome characterized by progressive accumulation of abundant gelatinous mucinous ascites and multifocal peritoneal implants throughout the abdominal cavity is **pseudomyxoma peritonei**. Arising almost exclusively from ruptured low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasms, expelled neoplastic goblet cells implant on peritoneal surfaces and continue producing voluminous jelly-like mucin, traditionally described as jelly belly.
steps.say: Pseudomyxoma peritonei involves progressive accumulation of jelly-like mucinous fluid following intraperitoneal rupture of an appendiceal neoplasm.

nodes.label: Transcoelomic Implantation of Mucin-Secreting Goblet Cells

steps.tx: The contemporary definitive curative treatment protocol for resectable pseudomyxoma peritonei combines complete surgical **cytoreductive surgery** with hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy. Pioneered by Paul Sugarbaker, the surgeon performs peritonectomy procedures to strip all affected peritoneal surfaces and resects involved viscera. This extirpation is immediately followed by ninety minutes of continuous perfusion with heated mitomycin C at forty-two degrees Celsius.
steps.say: Cytoreductive peritonectomy combined with hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy is the definitive curative treatment for pseudomyxoma peritonei.

rows: Peritoneal perfusion at 41 to 42 degrees Celsius
Hyperthermia increases tissue depth of chemotherapy
Mitomycin C or oxaliplatin instillation for 90 min
Direct cytotoxic destruction of microscopic floating cells
Restore digestive continuity safely after chemotherapy

steps.tx: The most common non-obstetric surgical emergency encountered during gestation is **appendicitis in pregnancy**, occurring in approximately one in one thousand pregnancies. Diagnosing appendicitis during pregnancy is notoriously difficult because common physiological symptoms of pregnancy, including nausea, vomiting, anorexia, and mild leukocytosis, mimic acute appendicitis. Delays in diagnosis carry severe hazards of perforation, fetal loss, and premature labor.
steps.say: Appendicitis is the most frequent non-obstetric surgical emergency in pregnancy, often delayed because symptoms mimic normal gestation.

steps.tx: The anatomical position of the appendix changes continuously throughout gestation as the expanding gravid uterus elevates and displaces the caecum. Beginning in the second trimester, the appendix is pushed progressively superiorly and laterally, so that by the **third trimester**, maximal pain and tenderness are localized to the right upper quadrant or flank, closely mimicking acute cholecystitis or pyelonephritis.
steps.say: The expanding gravid uterus pushes the appendix superiorly and laterally, shifting pain to the right upper quadrant by the third trimester.

nodes.label: First Trimester: Appendix in Standard Right Lower Quadrant
Second Trimester: Displaced Upward to Level of Umbilicus
Third Trimester: Pushed into Right Upper Quadrant / Flank
Atypical Pain Mimics Acute Cholecystitis or Pyelonephritis

steps.tx: Transabdominal graded-compression ultrasound is the first-line imaging modality of choice in pregnant women. When ultrasound is non-diagnostic or inconclusive, magnetic resonance imaging without intravenous gadolinium contrast is the definitive second-line modality, achieving a diagnostic accuracy exceeding ninety-five percent without exposing the fetus to ionizing **radiation hazard**. Non-contrast MRI clearly visualizes the inflamed, thickened appendiceal lumen.
steps.say: Ultrasound is the initial imaging modality in pregnancy, followed by non-contrast MRI to avoid ionizing radiation to the fetus.

rows: First-line screening; operator dependent in late pregnancy
Gold standard definitive imaging for inconclusive ultrasound
Reserved strictly when MRI unavailable and perforation suspected

steps.tx: Prompt open or laparoscopic appendicectomy is indicated upon clinical or radiological confirmation, with early surgery significantly reducing perforation rates. While uncomplicated appendicitis carries a fetal loss rate under two percent, perforated appendicitis with peritonitis causes fetal mortality rates to surge to twenty percent. Consequently, aggressive surgical intervention is prioritized, while elective **interval appendicectomy** is strictly deferred until several months postpartum.
steps.say: Prompt surgery prevents appendiceal perforation in pregnancy, avoiding fetal loss rates that reach twenty percent with peritonitis.
